correctness.rationale: The primary source supplies the smooth complete projective fan, nine ray-orbit representatives with stabilizers, and eight maximal-cone orbit representatives. With |Aut(A4)|=240, exact orbit--stabilizer arithmetic gives 400 rays. Exhaustion of all 240 signed coordinate permutations shows that each of the eight displayed maximal-cone representatives has trivial stabilizer and that their orbits are distinct, giving 1920 maximal cones. The toric divisor sequence gives Picard rank 400-4=396. Standard smooth projective toric cohomology gives odd Betti vanishing, Poincare duality, and Euler characteristic 1920, forcing b4=1126.

value.rationale: The model is a newly explicit smooth projective compactification introduced precisely to make birational and cohomological study of four-dimensional algebraic tori feasible. Its complete Betti profile and Picard rank are natural first invariants of that model, directly answering part of the paper's stated motivation toward cohomological invariants and Chow groups. The calculation is structural: it converts equivariant fan data into the full additive topology of the fourfold, rather than extracting an arbitrary small statistic.
